<<On Whitewashing A Cellar Wall This Season>>

This season, the neighborhood decided to tackle the aging cellar wall, a task that has been long overdue. The process began with a careful inspection, revealing layers of grime and mildew that had accumulated over the years. The team of volunteers, including local residents and a few handyman volunteers, worked together to remove the old, worn-out paint and prepare the surface for the new whitewash.

The whitewash, a mixture of lime, water, and a touch of food coloring, was applied in a way that not only refreshed the appearance of the wall but also provided a protective layer against the elements. The result was a clean, bright, and inviting look that brought a sense of renewal to the cellar.

The notice board was also updated with a reminder of the cleanup and maintenance efforts, ensuring that everyone was aware of the work done and the importance of keeping the cellar clean and safe.

P.P.S. Do not forget the notice board.
